title: Ask which end-to-end tests a change affects
statement: As a developer, I can ask which end-to-end tests a line of code or a range of code affects, so I know what to run to prove the stories it touches still work.
overview: Trevor's direction: "If I change this line of code, what e2e tests do I need to run to prove the affected stories are still functional?" Reviews and releases both work on code ranges, so they share one answer. `review test-plan` already walks a range this way, with a review as its only way in. `query traceability --ref` answers for a location, but only through accepted stories and slide Items, so it returned nothing for the lines tried here, including one with recorded test evidence. The tool answers the question, and people decide what to do with the answer.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Given one line of a file, the command lists the catalog entries to run if that line changes, without the line having been changed.
Given two revisions, the command gives the same answer for all the lines changed between them.
A review's range and a release's range, asked for by `review test-plan --e2e` and `release tests`, give the same tests as asking for that range directly.
An entry is listed when it verifies a criterion of a story the code reaches, once each, even if its own code did not change.
The walk follows slide Items and test-case evidence, and reaches proposed stories as well as accepted ones.
An entry whose own code is in the line or range is listed too.
Each listed test names the stories and criteria that selected it.
Retired and deprecated test cases are not listed.
The output says how many tests are listed and how many are in the catalog.
It does not drop a test because another seems to cover the same thing.
The command writes nothing and runs nothing.
